mods.note: "In 1854, a Statistical Office was set up within the Department of State to prepare an annual report on commercial relations of the United States with foreign nations. The agency name changed in 1874 to the Bureau of Statistics and again in 1897 to the Bureau of Foreign Commerce (to avoid confusion with other Statistics Bureaus). In 1903, the Bureau of Foreign Commerce and the Treasury Department's Bureau of Statistics were merged and transferred to the new Department of Commerce and Labor as the Bureau of Statistics for that executive department. This particular title, however, ended up under the auspices of the Manufactures Bureau under 1912 before moving to the Bureau of Foreign and Domestic Commerce in the Commerce Department." -- The College of Wooster Libraries, Congressional Serial Set Finding List: ﻿Annual Reports, Commercial Relations of the United States (S 4.1:, C 10.8:, C 18.16:)
﻿Issues for 1886-97 also contain data for the preceding year.﻿
